meta.name: New York City (Midtown Manhattan)
meta.scaleNote: game units per real metre; uniform, no compression
meta.originNote: centre of the play box: between Sixth and Seventh Aves at about 49th St
meta.axes: +X = east, -Z = north (true north up), +Y up. The Manhattan grid is rotated 28.9 deg clockwise of north: avenues run NNE-SSW (uptown = direction (0.483, -0.875)), streets ESE-WNW (east = (0.875, 0.483)). Matches the minimap (screen up = -Z).
meta.gridNote: Street-aligned rects have rot about -0.505 (local +X along the cross streets, ESE). Landmark front is a grid direction: west (WNW, toward the Hudson), east (ESE), uptown (NNE), downtown (SSW); frontDir is the world (x, z) unit vector.
meta.rotNote: All rot values are three.js rotation.y (radians). An object rotated by rot has its local +X axis pointing along (cos rot, -sin rot) in world (x, z). Building w is along local X, d along local Z.
meta.footprintNote: Footprints are CCW viewed from above (CCW in (x, -z)), open rings (first vertex not repeated). For THREE.Shape use (x, -z) then rotateX(-PI/2).
meta.heightNote: height / eaveHeight are game units (metres x 0.2). Landmarks: heightMetres = top of the structure incl. spires and masts; eaveMetres = main roof, or where the crown begins; nycRoofMetres = the NYC Open Data roof height of the matched footprint. Buildings: heightMetres from NYC height_roof; a merged block mass (merged = n footprints) takes the area-weighted height and keeps heightMaxMetres.
meta.mergeNote: NYC has 10,293 footprints in the box. Inside each tax block, touching buildings under 100 m within 2x of each other in height are merged while their union fills at least 62% of its grid-aligned rectangle and no side passes 120 m; slivers under 900 m2 fold into their nearest-height neighbour. Buildings of 100 m and more are never merged. footprint = the merged outline; cx/cz/w/d/rot = its grid-aligned rectangle (what the kit fills); height = area-weighted, heightMaxMetres = the tallest member. phoneSkip = small low rear-lot or interior structures.
meta.buildingFields: bin = NYC Building Identification Number of the main footprint; year = construction year (median for a merge); era = prewar (<1946) / postwar (1946-1989) / modern (1990+) for the kit and facade choice; onPier = stands on a Hudson or East River pier over water.
meta.projection: equirectangular about origin: x = (lon-lon0)*84437.8*scale, z = -(lat-lat0)*111049.3*scale (WGS84 metres per degree at lat0)
meta.source: NYC Open Data Building Footprints (dataset 5zhs-2jue, NYC Office of Technology and Innovation): footprints, roof heights, construction years. NYC 2015 Street Tree Census (uvpi-gqnh): street trees. OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), Overpass API snapshot 2026-11-15: coastline, roads, water, parks, paths, piers, bridges, building names, park trees. Landmark heights: CTBUH / Skyscraper Center and Wikipedia figures. Google Maps was not consulted: the Chrome extension was not connected.
meta.styleNote: style (generic buildings only): tenement = prewar walk-up / brownstone / tenement up to 24 m; prewar = prewar masonry (brick, limestone, terracotta, setbacks, water tanks) over 24 m; whitebrick = 1946-89 white / tan brick apartment or office block; glassslab = postwar or modern glass-and-metal slab; glasstower = 1990+ glass tower of 120 m and more. frontage = avenue (within 3 u of an avenue / Broadway) or street. zone = times_square / hudson_yards.

(St. Vartan Park Playground) Children's Play Area

bridges.name: Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge
bridges.desc: Queensboro Bridge (landmark queensboro_bridge): double-deck steel cantilever truss, 1909, dark grey-green riveted Warren trusses, finial-topped tower pinnacles about 107 m above the water, roadway about 41 m up. The West Channel span (299 m) crosses from the Manhattan anchorage at York Ave to Roosevelt Island.

buildings.name: Moynihan Train Hall (James A. Farley Building)
New York Public Library (Stephen A. Schwarzman Building)

landmarks.name: Empire State Building
landmarks.desc: The anchor of the south end of the map, 350 Fifth Ave between 33rd and 34th St. The 5-storey limestone base fills the whole lot (about 129 m along the streets x 57 m along Fifth Ave) with the main entrance under a shallow marquee on Fifth Ave. Above it the mass steps back at the 6th floor to a broad block, again at the 25th and 30th floors, then rises sheer as a tower about 40 x 60 m from the 30th to the 72nd floor; small setbacks at the 72nd and 81st floors lead to the 86th-floor open observation deck at 320 m, then the Art Deco mooring mast (a fluted aluminium-and-glass cylinder with four winged buttresses) to the 102nd-floor deck at 373 m and the antenna to 443 m. Facades: Indiana limestone and granite with continuous vertical chrome-nickel steel mullion strips between the window columns (the shaft reads as fine silver pinstripes), dark recessed aluminium spandrels, grey-tan overall. The top 30 floors are floodlit at night. It must read from every part of the map: the needle mast is the single most recognisable silhouette.

landmarks.name: Chrysler Building
landmarks.desc: 405 Lexington Ave at 42nd St, east of Grand Central. A lot about 61 x 62 m: a 16-storey base filling it, setbacks at the 16th, 23rd, 28th and 30th floors to a square shaft (about 30 m) with chamfered corners. White and grey brick with dark grey brick bands, wings of stylised radiator caps and hubcap friezes at the 31st floor, and the stainless-steel eagle gargoyles projecting from the four corners at the 61st floor. The crown is seven diminishing arched terraces of Nirosta stainless steel, each studded with triangular windows in a sunburst pattern, ending in a needle spire. The steel is bright silver and catches the afternoon sun; it should glint. Lit white along the arches at night.

landmarks.name: 30 Rockefeller Plaza (Comcast Building)
landmarks.desc: The centre of Rockefeller Center between Fifth and Sixth Aves, 49th to 50th St: a thin limestone slab about 31 m thick (along the avenues) and 100 m long (along the streets), 70 floors; its main front faces east onto Rockefeller Plaza and the Channel Gardens toward Fifth Ave, the low wing runs west to Sixth Ave. Its north and south faces step back in a series of narrow notches up the height so the slab reads like a stack of thin blades; the east and west ends rise almost sheer. Indiana limestone in vertical piers with recessed grey aluminium spandrels, so it reads as strong vertical stripes. Top of the Rock observation decks on the roof (glass screens), a GE/NBC logo frieze height. At its foot, east side: the gilded 'Wisdom' relief over the entrance; the sunken plaza with the skating rink and gilded Prometheus (rockefeller_rink), flags of the UN on poles round it, and the Channel Gardens running east to Fifth Ave between the two six-storey limestone pavilions (La Maison Francaise, the British Empire Building). The lower Rockefeller Center buildings (1230/1250/1270 Sixth Ave, the International Building with Atlas) are the same limestone family.

landmarks.name: One Vanderbilt
landmarks.desc: Madison to Vanderbilt Ave, 42nd to 43rd St, facing Grand Central across Vanderbilt Ave. The tallest tower on the east side: four interlocking tapering glass shafts, each sloping inward and stepping back at different heights so the tower narrows and twists as it rises, with a crystalline top and a slender spire to 427 m. Glass with ribbed white-ivory terracotta spandrels and soffits at each setback, the base corner cut away at 42nd and Vanderbilt to open a view of the terminal. Observation deck (SUMMIT) near the top with glass boxes cantilevered out.

landmarks.name: MetLife Building
landmarks.desc: 200 Park Ave, the slab that closes the vista up Park Avenue, standing directly north of Grand Central over its train shed. An elongated octagon in plan (about 91 m across the avenue x 46 m along it) with chamfered corners, 59 floors, on a 10-storey base that matches the terminal's cornice. Grey precast concrete mullions, vertical ribs and dark glass; two horizontal mechanical bands with recessed louvres at about the 21st and 46th floors; the huge METLIFE letters near the top on the north and south faces. Park Avenue's roadway runs through it at street level (the Helmsley Building portals just north) and wraps round Grand Central on the elevated Pershing Square viaduct.

landmarks.name: Grand Central Terminal
landmarks.desc: 42nd St between Vanderbilt and Lexington, Beaux-Arts 1913. The 42nd St (south) facade is the face: three enormous arched windows (about 18 m tall) between paired Doric columns, a central attic with the Tiffany clock and the sculpture group of Mercury, Hercules and Minerva on top (to about 46 m), the elevated Park Ave viaduct passing in front of it on a bridge across 42nd St and splitting round the building. Pink-grey Stony Creek granite base, buff Indiana limestone above, a green copper-roofed main concourse behind (about 84 x 37 m, roof about 38 m), lower wings east and west. The MetLife slab rises directly behind it and One Vanderbilt beside it to the west.

landmarks.name: United Nations Secretariat Building
landmarks.desc: On First Ave between 42nd and 46th St with the East River at its back: a pure 39-storey slab about 88 m long (along the avenue) and 22 m thick. The two broad faces (west to Manhattan, east to the river) are uninterrupted blue-green glass curtain walls with aluminium mullions; the narrow north and south ends are solid white Vermont marble with no windows. Two dark grilled mechanical bands at about the 6th floor and at the top. Before it on First Ave the row of 193 member flags on tall poles. Beside it the General Assembly building (un_general_assembly) and the low Conference Building along the river on FDR Drive's deck.

landmarks.name: United Nations General Assembly Building
landmarks.desc: North of the Secretariat: a long low building (about 115 x 50 m) with concave, sweeping side walls of white marble and a roof that dips in the middle like a saddle, the shallow dome over the Assembly Hall sitting off-centre on top. The north end (the visitors' entrance) is a glass wall facing the plaza and the lawn with the knotted-gun sculpture; landscaped lawns run north toward 48th St along the river.

landmarks.name: One Times Square
landmarks.desc: The narrow wedge at the south tip of Times Square where Broadway and Seventh Ave cross at 42nd-43rd St, 25 floors, about 30 x 18 m. Invisible as a building: every face above the ground floor is clad in stacked giant LED screens and billboards (bright, saturated, changing), the north face (looking up the square) most of all. A steel framework and flagpole on the roof carry the New Year's Eve ball (a 3.7 m crystal geodesic sphere) at 118 m. See times_square for the canyon.

landmarks.name: Times Square
landmarks.desc: The bow-tie where Broadway crosses Seventh Ave from 42nd to 47th St. Broadway is pedestrianised here (red-painted asphalt plazas with tables and chairs), Seventh Ave keeps its traffic. Every building facing the square has billboards and LED screens covering its lower 10-20 storeys, stacked and wrapped round corners (Coca-Cola, Samsung, Nasdaq's curved tower screen at 4 Times Square, the curved ribbon of 2 Times Square), with the red illuminated glass TKTS steps at Duffy Square (46th-47th) and the Father Duffy statue. It must glow even in daylight. nyc_times_square.json lists the buildings round the square and which faces carry signs.

landmarks.name: Bank of America Tower
landmarks.desc: One Bryant Park, Sixth Ave and 42nd St, facing Bryant Park across 42nd. A faceted crystalline glass tower: the plan is a square whose faces fold and taper in angled planes so the tower looks like a shard, with sloping slashes up the corners and a 77 m steel-and-glass spire offset on top (to 366 m). Clear low-iron glass, silver-white. The base has a glass atrium on the 42nd St / Sixth Ave corner and the restored Henry Miller's Theatre facade at its west end.

landmarks.name: The New York Times Building
landmarks.desc: 620 Eighth Ave between 40th and 41st St, facing west across Eighth Ave to the Port Authority Bus Terminal. A square-ish 52-storey glass tower (about 50 x 50 m with notched corners) wrapped on all four faces by a screen of horizontal white ceramic rods (about 186,000 of them) held off the glass, so it reads pale and finely striped, slightly transparent, changing colour with the sky; the rod screen runs past the roof line as an open grille, and a thin steel mast rises to 319 m. 'The New York Times' in blackletter across the Eighth Ave front at the base.

landmarks.name: Madison Square Garden
landmarks.desc: Seventh to Eighth Ave, 31st to 33rd St, on top of Penn Station. A drum about 130 m across and about 46 m tall with a shallow cable-suspended roof: precast concrete vertical ribs alternating with tall glass panels, a wide glass-fronted entrance pavilion on Seventh Ave (the Chase Square entrance with a large marquee screen showing events). Two Penn Plaza (a plain 30-storey dark slab, about 174 m) stands immediately east of it on Seventh Ave, the Moynihan Train Hall (the old Farley Post Office) across Eighth Ave to the west.

landmarks.name: 30 Hudson Yards (Edge)
landmarks.desc: The tallest of Hudson Yards, at the west end of 33rd St over the rail yards. A glass tower whose top is sliced off at a slant, with the Edge sky deck at 335 m: a triangular glass-floored prow cantilevered about 24 m out from the south-west corner, glass-walled, the tilted glass parapet visible from below. Faces of clear glass with fine vertical aluminium fins, the tower slightly tapering and canted at the top. Stands on the Hudson Yards platform with the Vessel in the plaza (vessel), the Shops podium (a curved 7-storey glass-and-limestone mall) at its foot, 10 Hudson Yards to the east and 35 / 50 / 15 Hudson Yards round the plaza.

landmarks.name: Vessel
landmarks.desc: The honeycomb in the middle of the Hudson Yards plaza: 154 interlocking flights of stairs and 80 landings forming a vase-shaped lattice, 15 m wide at the base widening to 46 m at the top, 45.7 m tall (16 storeys). Polished copper-coloured steel cladding on the underside of every flight (warm bronze-copper, reflective), concrete-grey treads and white handrails. Reads as a glowing copper basket.

landmarks.name: 432 Park Avenue
landmarks.desc: Park Ave between 56th and 57th St. A perfectly square pencil tower 28.5 x 28.5 m and 426 m tall (about 1:15), the flat top square with no crown. Exposed white architectural concrete grid: every face is a uniform 6 x 6 grid of 10 m square windows per floor-pair... visually a fine white grid of square dark windows, broken every 12 storeys by an open double-height mechanical floor (the wind breaks) where you can see through the tower, five of them. The tallest thing in the Billionaires' Row group east of Fifth.

landmarks.name: Central Park Tower
landmarks.desc: 225 West 57th St between Broadway and Seventh Ave, the tallest building on the map by roof (472 m). A glass tower with vertical white aluminium fins and a stepped silhouette: it steps back several times on the south side, cantilevers east at about the 30th floor over the neighbouring Art Students League, and ends in a flat top with a crown of glass fins. The Nordstrom store fills the glass base. Glass reads blue-silver with white vertical stripes.

landmarks.name: 111 West 57th Street (Steinway Tower)
landmarks.desc: The skinniest skyscraper in the world (about 18 x 60 m, 1:24), on 57th St between Fifth and Sixth Aves, rising behind the restored 16-storey 1925 Steinway Hall (limestone, a classical temple-topped tower of its own). The east and west faces are terracotta and bronze in vertical undulating piers, glass between; the south face steps back in a series of feathered setbacks so the top tapers to a thin blade. Warm cream-terracotta and bronze, a soft gold in the afternoon sun.

landmarks.name: One57
landmarks.desc: 157 West 57th St between Sixth and Seventh Aves. A glass tower in vertical stripes of two blues and silver (pixelated shades), with the curved 'waterfall' roofs: the top cascades down in a series of curved setbacks toward the north (Central Park) side. The base wraps the Park Hyatt.

landmarks.name: The Plaza Hotel
landmarks.desc: Fifth Ave at Central Park South (59th St), on the west side of Fifth Ave, its front facing east onto Grand Army Plaza with the Pulitzer Fountain and the gilded Sherman statue. A 20-storey French Renaissance chateau of white glazed brick and marble, an L-plan block with corner turrets and a steep green copper-and-slate mansard roof with dormers, gables and chimneys, flag poles over the Fifth Ave entrance under a canopy. Horse carriages lined up on Central Park South in front.

landmarks.name: St. Patrick's Cathedral
landmarks.desc: Fifth Ave between 50th and 51st St, facing west across Fifth to Rockefeller Center and Atlas. A Gothic Revival cruciform church about 101 m long (along the streets) x 53 m across the transept, of white Tuckahoe marble (bright, slightly warm): the west front has two lacy openwork spires to 100.6 m flanking a great rose window and pointed portals with bronze doors; flying buttresses, pinnacles and a steep grey slate roof along the nave, a Lady Chapel at the east (Madison Ave) end. Dwarfed by the towers round it (Olympic Tower behind).

landmarks.name: New York Public Library (Stephen A. Schwarzman Building)
landmarks.desc: Fifth Ave between 40th and 42nd St, Beaux-Arts 1911, facing east onto Fifth Ave (the back faces Bryant Park). About 120 m along Fifth and 107 m deep. White Vermont marble: a long front with a central portico of three tall arches between paired Corinthian columns, sculpture groups above, wide steps flanked by the two lions (Patience and Fortitude) and fountains, terraces with flagpoles and urns. The rear (west) facade on Bryant Park has tall narrow windows of the book stacks and the Main Reading Room's arched windows above.

landmarks.name: Bryant Park
landmarks.desc: The park behind the library between Fifth and Sixth Aves, 40th to 42nd St: a raised rectangular lawn about 70 x 90 m framed by double allees of London plane trees over gravel walks with movable green chairs, a balustrade, the Josephine Shaw Lowell fountain at the east and the carousel and grill at the north. The Bank of America Tower and W.R. Grace Building (curved white travertine) look down on it.

landmarks.name: Deutsche Bank Center
landmarks.desc: The former Time Warner Center on the west side of Columbus Circle: two identical 55-storey glass towers (229 m), parallelogram in plan, rising from a curved 10-storey base whose front follows the curve of the circle. Blue-green reflective glass with fine mullions, the space between the towers framed by a big glass atrium wall. Faces east toward the circle and Central Park.

landmarks.name: Columbus Circle and the Columbus Monument
landmarks.desc: The traffic circle at the south-west corner of Central Park where Broadway, Eighth Ave and Central Park West meet 59th St. In the middle a 23 m granite rostral column with bronze ships' prows, topped by a marble statue of Columbus, round a circular plaza with fountains and benches. At the park entrance (north-east side) the Maine Monument: a tall pylon topped by a gilded figure in a chariot of sea horses.

landmarks.name: Citigroup Center (601 Lexington)
landmarks.desc: Lexington Ave between 53rd and 54th St. A square tower (about 48 x 48 m) clad in bright silver-white aluminium and glass in horizontal bands, standing on four massive 35 m tall square stilts set at the middles of the sides (not the corners), so the corners are cantilevered over open air; St. Peter's Lutheran Church (a small granite block) sits under the north-west corner. The top is cut at a 45-degree slant facing south (the crown reads as a big sloping wedge from far away).

landmarks.name: Lever House
landmarks.desc: 390 Park Ave at 53rd St, 1952. A slender 24-storey slab of blue-green tinted glass and stainless steel mullions (about 16 m thick), standing at right angles to Park Ave on the north part of its lot, raised on a 1-storey hovering horizontal podium on pilotis that covers the lot and leaves an open plaza underneath. Crisp, light, mint-green glass.

landmarks.name: Seagram Building
landmarks.desc: 375 Park Ave between 52nd and 53rd St, Mies van der Rohe 1958. A 38-storey bronze-and-dark-amber-glass slab set 30 m back from Park Ave behind a pink granite plaza with two rectangular fountain pools and low marble benches; non-structural bronze I-beam mullions running the full height, bronze-tinted glass, a back spine block behind. Dark, brown-bronze, very sober.

landmarks.name: Radio City Music Hall
landmarks.desc: Sixth Ave at 50th St, the corner of Rockefeller Center. An Art Deco limestone-faced block with the famous vertical neon sign 'RADIO CITY' (red letters on a tall rounded blade, six storeys) at the corner and the rounded marquee wrapping the corner of Sixth and 50th in bands of red-and-blue neon with white running lights. The 1270 Sixth Ave office tower (31 storeys, 140 m, limestone) rises on the same block behind it.

landmarks.name: Carnegie Hall
landmarks.desc: Seventh Ave at 57th St, 1891 Italian Renaissance: a 6-storey hall of russet-brown Roman brick with terracotta trim, arched windows, a five-arch loggia entrance on 57th St under a terracotta frieze, the studio tower wings (13-16 storeys) behind. The thin dark Carnegie Hall Tower (231 m, brick-red with dark bands) rises right beside it on 57th St.

landmarks.name: Queensboro Bridge
landmarks.desc: The double-deck steel cantilever bridge from 59th/60th St over the East River and Roosevelt Island to Queens, 1909. In this box: the Manhattan approach on stone-and-steel piers from Second Ave, the Manhattan anchorage tower (a steel truss tower on a granite pier at York Ave), the 299 m West Channel cantilever span and the Roosevelt Island tower (the east spans to Queens are past the box edge and belong to the surround). Heavy dark grey-green riveted Warren trusses with ornate finial-topped pinnacles on the towers (about 107 m above the water), the roadway about 41 m above the river. The vaulted Guastavino tile arcade under the Manhattan approach (Bridgemarket) at 59th St.

landmarks.name: 10 Hudson Yards
landmarks.desc: The first Hudson Yards tower at Tenth Ave and 30th St, straddling the High Line's spur. Glass with angled faceted planes, the top cut at a slope facing east, a 'stacked' base.

landmarks.name: 35 Hudson Yards
landmarks.desc: North-west of the plaza at 11th Ave and 33rd St. Limestone-and-glass tower with a stepped silhouette of vertical cream stone fins, setbacks near the top.

landmarks.name: 50 Hudson Yards
landmarks.desc: Tenth Ave at 33rd-34th St, a broad glass tower with a stone-clad grid and four stacked tiers that step in.

landmarks.name: 15 Hudson Yards
landmarks.desc: West side of the plaza beside the Shed: a glass tower that rises from a rectangle and twists into a rounded crown of four petal-like glass lobes, a latticed open crown on top.

landmarks.name: The Shed
landmarks.desc: Arts centre beside 15 Hudson Yards: a fixed 8-storey building and a telescoping shell of exposed steel diagrid with quilted translucent ETFE cushions (milky white) that rolls out on rails over the plaza.

landmarks.name: One Manhattan West
landmarks.desc: Ninth Ave at 33rd St over the rail cut: a glass tower with tapering chamfered corners and a slightly flared top, the glass curving out at the base.

landmarks.name: Two Manhattan West
landmarks.desc: South of One Manhattan West at 31st St: a glass tower whose west face slopes back in a long curve.

landmarks.name: The Spiral (66 Hudson Boulevard)
landmarks.desc: Tenth Ave at 34th St: a glass tower that steps back in a continuous ascending spiral of planted terraces (green ledges wrapping round it as it rises).

landmarks.name: Jacob K. Javits Convention Center
landmarks.desc: Eleventh to Twelfth Ave, 34th to 40th St: a huge low exhibition hall about 300 x 140 m under a steel space-frame of dark reflective glass cubes (a 'crystal palace'), stepped pyramidal glass halls over the entrances on Eleventh Ave, a green roof.

landmarks.name: USS Intrepid (Intrepid Museum, Pier 86)
landmarks.desc: An Essex-class aircraft carrier moored along Pier 86 at West 46th St, 266 m long with a 45 m wide flight deck about 17 m above the water, lying along the north side of the pier (w = length, along the cross streets), bow to the west. Haze-grey hull and island superstructure with mast and radar on the starboard (north) side, jets and helicopters parked on the deck, the space shuttle Enterprise pavilion (a white inflatable dome-like shed) at the aft end; the submarine Growler alongside the pier.

landmarks.name: Moynihan Train Hall (James A. Farley Building)
landmarks.desc: Eighth to Ninth Ave, 31st to 33rd St, McKim Mead & White 1912: a long granite Corinthian colonnade (20 columns) on Eighth Ave on top of a broad flight of steps, the inscription 'Neither snow nor rain...' in the frieze; the new glass-and-steel skylight vaults of the train hall rising from the courtyard.

landmarks.name: One Penn Plaza
landmarks.desc: Eighth Ave at 34th St, north of the Garden: a 57-storey plain dark-bronze glass and aluminium tower, ribbed.

landmarks.name: One Worldwide Plaza
landmarks.desc: Eighth Ave between 49th and 50th St: a brick-and-cast-stone postmodern tower with setbacks and a copper pyramid roof (green) crowned by a frosted glass lantern that glows at night.

landmarks.name: Hearst Tower
landmarks.desc: Eighth Ave at 57th St: a glass-and-steel diagrid tower (triangular facets, the corners bevelled into 'birds' mouths') rising out of the hollowed-out 6-storey 1928 Art Deco cast-stone Hearst base with its allegorical statues.

landmarks.name: 220 Central Park South
landmarks.desc: Limestone-clad tower on Central Park South with a stepped silhouette, arched windows and a top of narrowing tiers; cream stone, traditional.

landmarks.name: 53W53 (MoMA Tower)
landmarks.desc: West 53rd St beside MoMA: a needle-thin tapering tower wrapped in a dark irregular diagrid of exposed structure, the facets narrowing to several pointed peaks at the top.

landmarks.name: Trump Tower
landmarks.desc: 725 Fifth Ave at 56th St: a 58-storey dark bronze glass tower with sawtooth faceted corners and a stepped series of planted terraces at its lower floors on Fifth Ave.

landmarks.name: General Motors Building
landmarks.desc: 767 Fifth Ave at 58th-59th St facing Grand Army Plaza: a 50-storey white Georgia marble slab with continuous vertical marble piers and recessed dark windows, a sunken plaza in front with the Apple Fifth Avenue glass cube (apple_cube).

landmarks.name: 4 Times Square (One Five Five)
landmarks.desc: Broadway and 42nd-43rd St on the east side of the square: a 48-storey tower, the Times Square faces glass and steel with the curved Nasdaq LED tower wrapping the Broadway / 43rd corner over 7 storeys, the Sixth Ave side stone; a lattice antenna to 351 m.

landmarks.name: Paramount Building
landmarks.desc: 1501 Broadway at 43rd-44th St, west side of the square: a buff limestone Art Deco ziggurat of setbacks, a four-faced clock near the top and a glass globe on the summit.

landmarks.name: 270 Park Avenue (JPMorgan Chase)
landmarks.desc: Park Ave between 47th and 48th St (2025): a 60-storey tower of tapered fanning steel columns at its base (a tall open hall), glass faces in vertical stainless fins, stepping back in four tiers toward the top with a crown of fins and wind turbines.

landmarks.name: 425 Park Avenue
landmarks.desc: Park Ave at 55th-56th St: a glass tower stepping back twice with tapered columns, the top a lantern of three vertical blades.

landmarks.name: Helmsley Building
landmarks.desc: 230 Park Ave, straddling Park Ave immediately north of the MetLife Building: a Beaux-Arts limestone tower with two arched road tunnels through its base, a stepped body and an ornate pyramidal copper roof with a gilded cupola, floodlit gold.

landmarks.name: Waldorf Astoria New York
landmarks.desc: 301 Park Ave between 49th and 50th St: Art Deco limestone hotel, a broad block with a twin tower that ends in two copper-capped spires, set back above a long Park Ave front.

landmarks.name: Chanin Building
landmarks.desc: Lexington Ave and 42nd St across from the Chrysler: brick-and-terracotta Art Deco tower with setback buttresses and a scalloped terracotta crown.

landmarks.name: Trump World Tower
landmarks.desc: First Ave at 47th St across from the UN: a plain 72-storey slab of dark bronze glass, flat-topped.

landmarks.name: 731 Lexington (Bloomberg Tower)
landmarks.desc: Lexington Ave at 58th-59th St: a glass tower on a broad block, the upper tower set on the east side, a glass-roofed courtyard in the middle.

landmarks.name: 550 Madison Avenue
landmarks.desc: Madison Ave at 55th-56th St: pink-grey granite postmodern tower with a 'Chippendale' broken pediment crown with a circular cutout, a seven-storey arched entrance on Madison.

landmarks.name: 383 Madison Avenue
landmarks.desc: Madison Ave at 46th-47th St: granite-and-glass octagonal tower on a square base, an octagonal glass crown lit at night.

landmarks.name: Macy's Herald Square
landmarks.desc: Broadway and Seventh Ave between 34th and 35th St: a whole-block 1902 store of brown brick and limestone (9 storeys on Broadway, the 1924-31 Seventh Ave wing rising to 19 storeys, 98 m) with a classical Broadway front, the red star and 'Macy's' signs, awnings; Herald Square's little triangle park in front with the bell-ringers clock.

landmarks.name: Metropolitan Opera House (Lincoln Center)
landmarks.desc: Lincoln Center Plaza at Columbus Ave and 63rd-64th St: a travertine box fronted by five tall arches of glass (the Chagall murals visible inside), facing east over the plaza and the Revson Fountain, flanked by David Geffen Hall and the David H. Koch Theater (both travertine colonnaded boxes).

landmarks.name: International Building and Atlas
landmarks.desc: Rockefeller Center's Fifth Ave tower (630 Fifth, 41 storeys) facing St Patrick's: limestone with vertical piers, the 14 m bronze Atlas holding the armillary sphere in its forecourt on Fifth Ave.

landmarks.name: Rockefeller Center Rink and Prometheus
landmarks.desc: The sunken plaza at the foot of 30 Rock: an oval-cornered rink (ice in winter, cafe tables in summer) about 40 x 30 m below street level, the gilded bronze Prometheus (5.5 m) reclining over a fountain at the west end, a ring of flagpoles round the top edge.

landmarks.name: Bethesda Terrace and Fountain
landmarks.desc: Central Park at 72nd St: a two-level sandstone terrace with carved balustrades and twin grand stairs down to a lake-side plaza with the Angel of the Waters fountain (bronze angel on a two-tier basin, 8 m) and the Lake beyond; the Mall's elm allee arrives at the top from the south.

landmarks.name: Wollman Rink
landmarks.desc: Central Park near 62nd St: a large rounded-rectangle skating rink (white ice in winter) with a low rink house, the Midtown skyline (Billionaires' Row) towering behind it to the south.

landmarks.name: Roosevelt Island Tramway (Manhattan station)
landmarks.desc: Second Ave at 59th-60th St: the Manhattan terminal and a tall steel lattice tower carrying the red cable cars east over the Queensboro Bridge's side and the river to Roosevelt Island, cables rising to about 76 m.

landmarks.name: The New Yorker Hotel
landmarks.desc: Eighth Ave at 34th St: Art Deco brick setback tower with the tall red 'NEW YORKER' sign on its roof.

landmarks.name: Apple Fifth Avenue cube
landmarks.desc: A 10 m clear glass cube with a hanging white Apple logo in the GM Building plaza.

landmarks.name: Pulitzer Fountain (Grand Army Plaza)
landmarks.desc: Tiered granite fountain basins topped by the bronze Pomona, in front of the Plaza Hotel; the gilded Sherman equestrian statue (Victory leading him) just north.

landmarks.name: William Tecumseh Sherman Monument
landmarks.desc: Bright gilded equestrian group on a pink granite pedestal.

landmarks.name: Gapstow Bridge
landmarks.desc: A small arched schist footbridge over the north end of the Pond.

landmarks.name: Tavern on the Green
landmarks.desc: A Victorian Gothic former sheepfold of red-brown brick with slate roofs and a glass pavilion, by Central Park West at 67th St.

landmarks.name: Central Park Zoo
landmarks.desc: Brick-arcaded zoo buildings round a sea-lion pool, the Arsenal and the Delacorte clock.

landmarks.name: TKTS red steps (Duffy Square)
landmarks.desc: A glowing red glass staircase (bleachers) at the north tip of Times Square, the TKTS booth under it.

landmarks.name: Daily News Building
landmarks.desc: 220 East 42nd St: white brick Art Deco slab with dark-red striped piers and a flat top; a giant globe in the lobby.

landmarks.name: Port Authority Bus Terminal
landmarks.desc: Eighth Ave 40th-42nd St: a long grey steel-framed bus terminal with ramps to the Lincoln Tunnel on its west side.

landmarks.name: Pepsi-Cola sign (Gantry Plaza)
landmarks.desc: Long Island City waterfront, across the East River from the UN: the red neon 'Pepsi-Cola' script and bottle on a steel frame, facing Manhattan; the black steel gantry cranes of Gantry Plaza State Park beside it.

landmarks.name: Central Synagogue
landmarks.desc: Lexington Ave at 55th St: Moorish Revival brownstone with two octagonal towers capped by green-and-gold onion domes.

landmarks.name: St. Bartholomew's Church
landmarks.desc: Park Ave at 50th-51st St: Byzantine Revival salmon brick and limestone with a tiled polychrome dome, set back behind a terrace.

landmarks.name: Herald Square bell clock (James Gordon Bennett Monument)
landmarks.desc: Herald Square: bronze Minerva with two bell-ringers who strike a bell on the hour, on a granite base.

player.note: Rises from the Hudson off the Intrepid and Pier 84 (about W 44th St) and wades ashore east-south-east up the cross streets toward Times Square, the Bank of America Tower, One Vanderbilt and the Chrysler; the Empire State Building stands off to the right (south-east). rot = rotation.y that turns a +Z-forward model to face the facing vector.

ring.note: Title Match ring on Sheep Meadow, Central Park (66th-69th St between the West Drive and the Mall): the open lawn with the Central Park South skyline (Central Park Tower, 111 W 57th, One57, 432 Park) behind it to the south and the Mall's elm allee to the east. The venue box (venueBox [minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ], Chicago venue x -58..+48, z -50..+50 about the ring centre) is axis-aligned while the park runs at 29 deg, so its corners reach the West Drive and the 65th St transverse road; no landmark is inside it (Tavern on the Green is west of it, Wollman Rink south, Bethesda Terrace north). The small park structures in it (removedSmallStructures: comfort stations, the Chess & Checkers House / Dairy class of buildings, all under 13 m) are left out of the layout, and nyc_trees.json leaves out every tree within ringClearTrees. clear = half-size of the largest axis-aligned square free of buildings and props. A search of the whole box (site_search.py) finds no other place where even a 60 x 60 u square is free of buildings: Central Park is the only home for the Chicago venue.

alternatives.note: Central Park, the same meadow shifted east onto the Mall and the Naumburg Bandshell: the venue box then takes 7 park structures (the bandshell, the kiosks on the Mall) and the south half of the elm allee; worse than the chosen site

the Western Rail Yard at Hudson Yards (the open platform west of 11th Ave, 30th-33rd St, the Vessel and 35 / 15 Hudson Yards just east): open ground about 40 u square, so a ring of half about 19 u, not the Chicago venue
Bryant Park lawn behind the Library: only about 70 x 90 m of lawn between plane-tree allees; a ring of half 6-7 u at most, so not the Chicago venue

a.note: player: the Bryant Park lawn behind the Library, facing uptown toward Central Park

b.note: rival: Central Park by the Heckscher Ballfields and the Pond, facing downtown toward Bryant Park

duel.note: VS Duel: the two kaiju face each other across Midtown, about 369 u apart through the Sixth Ave canyon (findOpenSpawn searches 20 u round each).

soldier.note: Lone Soldier start: the Times Square pedestrian plaza on Broadway at about 44th St, facing downtown (SSW) toward One Times Square and its screens, with the billboard canyon all round.
